correctness.rationale: For alpha>-1, an exact n-fold derivative factorization yields a positive prefactor multiplied by 1+alpha product_i u_i(2+alpha u_i). For alpha<0, every factor increases on [0,1], making the all-one corner exactly decisive; if negative there, a negative-density interior box disproves the copula. The unimodal function s(2-s)^n has exactly one subunit threshold root; this proves the complete range. Algebraic CDF factorization proves the positive two-component product mixture, and Hoeffding covariance plus nonnegative variances exclude infinite exchangeable negative-covariance margins. SymPy identities and rational/high-precision examples (51 assertions) support, but do not replace, the all-n proof. The alpha<=-1 pole/discontinuity is handled.

value.rationale: Admissibility is foundational for actual probability applications of the published n-variate model. The exact complete parameter domain enlarges the permissible negative-dependence range; N(s) quantifies an otherwise hidden maximum dimension of the specified finite model. The nonnegative region has a constructive binary latent-factor interpretation usable at arbitrary dimension, whereas negative pairwise covariance precludes any infinite exchangeable extension. This is a natural exact classification with structural consequences, rather than an arbitrary finite check or a precision-only update.
